questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Labor demand from marginal revenue product
questions.stem: A train dispatcher notes a firm hires labor until marginal revenue product equals the wage; why does labor demand slope downward?

options.text: Because marginal product of labor falls as more labor is hired
Because the wage always rises with output

options.misconception: confuses fixed costs with labor demand

questions.explanation: Diminishing marginal product makes marginal revenue product fall as labor rises, so the firm hires less at higher wages. The distractors invoke wage or cost behavior instead.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Output rises from 40 to 46 units when labor rises from 8 to 9 workers; what is the marginal product of the ninth worker?
questions.explanation: Marginal product is the change in output divided by the change in labor, which is 6 divided by 1 equals 6. The value is the extra output of that worker.
questions.hint: Divide output change by worker change

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A worker's marginal product is 5 units and the price of output is 4 dollars; what is the marginal revenue product?
questions.explanation: Marginal revenue product equals marginal product times price, which is 5 times 4 equals 20. This is the revenue added by the worker.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: In a competitive labor market, equilibrium occurs where which two curves intersect?

options.misconception: confuses product market with labor market
confuses firm totals with market equilibrium

questions.explanation: Labor market equilibrium is where labor supply equals labor demand. The distractors use product-market or firm-level conditions.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: The hiring rule of a competitive firm
questions.stem: A competitive firm maximizes profit by hiring labor until what condition holds?

options.text: Marginal revenue product equals the wage

questions.explanation: The firm hires until the revenue from the last worker equals the wage. The distractors use averages or break-even conditions.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: If output price rises, what happens to labor demand?
questions.explanation: Higher output price raises marginal revenue product, shifting labor demand right. The distractors reverse the effect or confuse curves.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A dispatcher compares pay over time; what makes a wage increase a real wage increase?

options.text: The nominal wage rises at all

questions.explanation: A real wage increase requires nominal pay to grow faster than prices. Nominal growth alone, employer revenue or hours do not suffice.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A dangerous job pays more than a safe job with the same skill; what explains the gap?

options.misconception: confuses market power with risk pay

questions.explanation: The extra pay compensates for job disamenities such as risk. Monopsony, discrimination and unions are different explanations.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Clearing of a competitive labor market
questions.stem: If the wage is above equilibrium, what happens in a competitive labor market?

options.text: A surplus of labor and unemployment

questions.explanation: A wage above equilibrium creates excess labor supply and unemployment. The distractors reverse or deny the imbalance.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A single large employer dominates a town's labor market; what is this called?

options.misconception: confuses few sellers with one buyer

questions.explanation: A single buyer of labor is a monopsony. Monopoly, oligopoly and perfect competition describe seller-side or many-buyer markets.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A monopsonist hires labor until marginal revenue product equals what?
questions.explanation: The monopsonist sets MRP equal to marginal factor cost, not the wage. The distractors apply the competitive rule or use averages.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: In monopsony, the wage paid is determined by what?

options.text: The labor supply curve at the chosen employment

questions.explanation: The monopsonist pays the wage on the supply curve at the employment level chosen. MFC, MRP and average product do not set the wage.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Why is marginal factor cost above the wage in monopsony?

options.text: Because hiring more requires raising the wage for all workers

options.misconception: confuses fixed costs with labor cost

questions.explanation: To hire an extra worker the monopsonist must raise the wage for all workers, so MFC exceeds the wage. Product, price or fixed costs do not explain it.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A monopsonist pays a wage below marginal revenue product; what is this called?
questions.explanation: Paying less than MRP is monopsonistic exploitation. Efficiency wages, differentials and union rents are different concepts.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Compared with the competitive level, a monopsonist hires fewer workers; why?

options.text: Because wages are fixed by law

questions.explanation: Since MFC exceeds the wage, the monopsonist stops hiring before the competitive level. MRP is not zero and supply is not vertical.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Monopsony creates deadweight loss because employment is below the level where MRP equals what?
questions.explanation: Efficiency requires MRP to equal the wage; monopsony stops where MRP equals MFC, so employment is too low. The distractors use monopsony or product measures.
questions.hint: MRP equals wage at efficient level

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Read employment from MRP and MFC table
questions.stem: Using the table, how many workers does the monopsonist hire?
questions.explanation: Hire while MRP is at least MFC: 30>=12, 24>=16, 18>=20 false, so 3 workers. The distractors stop too early or too late.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A minimum wage is binding when it is set above what?
questions.explanation: A minimum wage binds only if set above the equilibrium wage. Productivity or cost measures do not define binding.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Employment under a binding minimum wage
questions.learningObjective: Explain employment effect of binding minimum wage
questions.stem: In a competitive market, a binding minimum wage above equilibrium leads to what?

options.text: A surplus of labor and lower employment
Higher wages for all with same employment

questions.explanation: A binding minimum wage raises the wage and reduces employment, creating a labor surplus. The distractors reverse or deny the effect.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A policymaker sets a minimum wage just below equilibrium; what is the result?

options.misconception: applies binding outcome to nonbinding case

options.text: No binding effect on employment or wages

questions.explanation: A minimum wage below equilibrium is nonbinding and has no effect. The distractors apply binding outcomes incorrectly.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A minimum wage set between the monopsony wage and MRP can have what effect in monopsony?
questions.explanation: In monopsony a moderate minimum wage can raise wages and employment by removing the MFC wedge. The distractors apply competitive or no-effect outcomes.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Reading a minimum wage employment table

stimulus.body: Wage 8,10,12 with labor supply 20,24,28 and demand 28,24,20.

questions.stem: Using the table, what is employment at a minimum wage of 12?
questions.explanation: At a wage of 12, firms demand 20 workers, so employment is 20. Supply is 28, creating a surplus. The distractors use supply or equilibrium.

Risk gap compensating, bias gap discriminatory

questions.topic: Labor demand from marginal revenue product

answer.exemplar: As more labor is hired, marginal product falls, so marginal revenue product falls; the firm hires less at higher wages, making labor demand downward sloping.

questions.explanation: Diminishing marginal product reduces MRP as employment rises. The explanation links productivity to hiring decisions.
